rows.text: I like this, however, because it lets me glance at the time before it unlocks. Cons: Small screen (but hey, if you wanted a bigger screen, you wouldn't be looking at this phone) That's it! I use this phone pretty heavily, and I still get a full day of use out of it. Bonus: battery cases for the 5s fit the SE and are relatively cheap (~$25), so if you're a super heavy user, I highly recommend investing in one for even longer battery life! The performance never ceases to amaze me with the A9 chip and 2GB of RAM. Games load quickly and play smoothly, apps switch seamlessly, and nothing ever crashes. It's a silky smooth experience. Seriously, if you're in the market for a smaller phone, get this! It will be supported until at least iOS 11, and probably much longer.

Struggling one year in. Started off great, with 100% battery capacity, totally clean with no scratches, dents, or problems at all. But, I’ve now had the phone for a year and the battery life has fallen off a cliff (much faster than the last iPhone I bought new) and it has started freezing up during regular use. Will be stretches of 5-10 seconds where the screen freezes, and these are happening about every other day. No way of knowing if I just got unlucky or if these refurbs aren’t meant to last long.

A little lagging. It's a good phone - it does everything it's supposed to. This one was refurbished, so I noticed a few things that were unusual. There is this lag time (delay) between when I begin typing a text message and before it actually appears on screen. This doesn't happen all the time, but when it does, it's super annoying. I also noticed that the battery life of my 7+ was way longer than this phone, so I don't know what happened in the refurbishing process. Other than that, it's a nice, comfortable-to-hold phone, not too heavy at all, and easy to watch shows/movies on. It fits well in my pocket unlike my 7+, and is not cumbersome like the 12 Pro Max.

Why I'm keeping the iPhone SE. 7 Months ago, someone asked me what I thought of my S6 Edge by Samsung. I said I loved it. Why? Big screen, high resolution, awesome camera(which my girlfriend absolutely loved), and a cool edge feature that everyone (not so much) was jealous of. I might not have mentioned; the terrible battery life, lag, and dependability issues. About a month ago, it started acting up... turning off, lagging up, and in general just... becoming a piece of crap. Not to mention, the 5 hour battery life. All this... on a flagship device not even a year old. And I treat my phone alright. So I started doing some research, did you know when you search Google for Samsung problems, you get 627,000 results? I'm sure all android users are acclimatized with that feeling, of needing to upgrade every 5-6 months.

Its very innovative and convenient. I do have a few knocks, and the main one has to do with the fact that the backwards key (to go back to the last page, or back out of an app like facebook, messenger, etc.) when on the internet is not always in the same place like my android, which has a dedicated backwards button. This means I have to scour the screen, looking for where I should tap to go back t the previous page. So therefore because of my lack of experience, I have trouble backing out of apps with the same speed I can do other things on the phone. Its a small knock, because that will cease with me getting used to the phone.

Like Brand New. Phone came as advertised and looked brand new. Mine charges to the full 100% and there were no visible dings, scratches, or damage. The increased power allows for web pages to load much faster, it has far less app crashes, and if you have multiple tabs open on Safari, they don’t need to constantly reload when you switch between them. Many times if you are watching a video in one tab and stop it halfway through, if you come back to view it later, it will pick back up right where you left the videos which older iPhones definitely would not do. It does not get the 3D touch functionality as the 6S did and comes in 16GB and 64GB storage sizes. It has the same A9 chip as the iPhone 6S and can be upgraded to IOS 10. The software is clean, smooth, and works well.

Apple quality and not bulky at a great price. Works great. Just as expected. No lagging or freezing. Great price for what you get. If you don’t mind not having the fancy camera, this is a great choice. This is much smaller too so it actually fits in your pocket.

The Perfect iPhone. This phone is amazing in terms of performance and battery life. It can run Pokémon Go with music playing and a dozen background apps open without a hiccup and while consuming less battery than you would expect. As a long time iPod and iPhone customer this has exceeded all of my expectations.

The smaller 4inch screen can be a great pro or a con depending on what you like and your hand size, but as an average guy it's fine to me. I personally can't stand a phone to lag and glitch on me so I grew to have a great disdain for all the androids I had over time... as I've gotten older I just want a phone to work and have good quality pictures so I grew to love how simple ios is, and also grew to love the good camera as well.
